title: 1966 AHSME Problem 22
statement:
Consider the statements:

\[ \text{(I) }\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=0 \] \[ \text{(II) }\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=ab \] \[ \text{(III) }\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=a+b \] \[ \text{(IV) }\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=a-b \]

where we allow \(a\) and \(b\) to be real or complex numbers. Those statements for which there exist solutions other than \(a=0\) and \(b=0,\) are:

solutions.text:
Every statement has a nonzero solution. For \((\mathrm{I}),\) use \((a,b)=(1,i).\) For \((\mathrm{II}),\) use \(a=b=\sqrt2,\) giving \(\sqrt4=2=ab.\) For both \((\mathrm{III})\) and \((\mathrm{IV}),\) use \((a,b)=(1,0).\) Thus all four statements qualify.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: One nonzero example is enough for each statement
Try \(b=i\) for \((\mathrm{I}),\) equal positive values for \((\mathrm{II}),\) and \(b=0\) for \((\mathrm{III})\) and \((\mathrm{IV})\)
